bib.title: Back to Basics: Revisiting REINFORCE Style Optimization for Learning from Human Feedback in LLMs

question: Can the computational and optimization complexity of PPO be avoided in RLHF for LLMs while preserving performance?
hypothesis: Because the policy starts from a strong pretrained/SFT model, high variance and large off-policy updates are rare, so PPO's variance reduction, clipping and per-token modelling are unnecessary and REINFORCE-style methods suffice.
contributions: PPO is not the right tool: Vanilla PG REINFORCE outperforms PPO by 3.2% to 20.3% win-rate.
RLOO outperforms PPO, DPO and RAFT across datasets and models and uses online samples better than RAFT.
Modeling partial completions is not necessary; modeling the full generation preserves performance with less complexity.
RLOO is relatively robust to noise and KL penalty compared with RAFT.

method.summary: Ablates PPO on RLHF (GAE lambda, clipping, ratio) and compares full-generation-as-one-action REINFORCE (moving-average baseline) and RLOO (k=2, 4) against PPO, Vanilla PG, RAFT and DPO on TL;DR and Anthropic-HH with Pythia-6.9B and Llama-7B. Evaluates reward-model reward, GPT-4 simulated win-rates, fluency/diversity and robustness to KL weight and reward noise.

datasets.name: TL;DR Summarize (Stiennon et al., 2020)
datasets.size: 116k human-written instructions and 93k human-annotated preference pairs (training split)
datasets.split: dedicated SFT split for SFT; 1000 test samples for evaluation

datasets.name: Anthropic Helpful and Harmless (Bai et al., 2022a)
datasets.split: no SFT split: prompts and preferred responses from the comparisons used for SFT; 1000 test samples for evaluation

models.name: Pythia-6.9B
models.init_from: pretrained, then SFT; reward model and policy both initialised from the SFT checkpoint

models.name: Llama-7B
models.init_from: pretrained, then SFT; reward model and policy both initialised from the SFT checkpoint

training.objective: SFT cross-entropy; reward model binary classifier on preference pairs; RL stage maximises reward minus beta*KL to reference with PPO, Vanilla PG, REINFORCE (moving-average baseline), RLOO (k=2,4), RAFT (best of k) or DPO
training.lr: SFT Pythia 2e-5; RM 1e-5; preference training constant 1e-6
training.lr_schedule: SFT and RM: cosine decay; preference training: constant after linear warm-up
training.warmup: SFT/RM 0.03 ratio; preference training 3% of total steps
training.batch_size: TL;DR and HH-Pythia: rollout batch 512, step batch 256; HH-Llama: 2048 rollout and step batch
training.steps: TL;DR 600 steps; HH Pythia 393 steps; HH Llama 2 epochs
training.epochs: SFT Pythia 2, SFT Llama 1; RM 1; HH Llama preference training 2
training.regularisation: KL penalty beta = 0.03 for TL;DR, beta = 0.10 for all Anthropic-HH unless noted; 2 gradient steps per batch

other.lr_sweep: {1e-6, 1e-5, 2e-5} for RAFT and RLOO; {1e-6, 1e-5} for PPO and Vanilla PG

inference.decoding: greedy sampling at evaluation unless noted
inference.samples: 1000 test prompts per evaluation; k online samples per prompt in training (k=2 or 4 for RLOO and RAFT)
inference.prompting: TL;DR: 'Below is a reddit POST and the corresponding SUBREDDIT and TITLE. Write a both precise and concise summary of the contents of the post.'; HH: 'Human: ... Assistant:'

metrics.name: Average test reward
metrics.definition: mean reward from the training RM on 1000 test samples

metrics.name: Simulated win-rate
metrics.definition: GPT-4 (AlpacaFarm) preference vs reference SFT completions (TL;DR) or preferred completions (HH); checkpoint with highest test reward

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: perplexity on preferred completions of the test set

eval.protocol: Single reported run per cell; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests stated; GPT-4 as proxy for human evaluation.

prompts.text: Which of the following summaries does a better job of summarizing the most important points in the given forum post, without including unimportant or irrelevant details? A good summary is both precise and concise. Post: {instruction} Summary (A): {output_1} Summary (B): {output_2} FIRST provide a one-sentence comparison of the two summaries, explaining which you prefer and why. SECOND, on a new line, state only "Summary (A)" or " Summary (B)" to indicate your choice.

For the following query to a chatbot assistant, which response is more helpful? Query: instruction Response (A): {output_1} Response (B): {output_2} FIRST provide a one-sentence comparison of the two responses and explain which you feel is more helpful. SECOND, on a new line, state only "Response (A)" or "Response (B)" to indicate which response is more helpful. If they are equally good or bad, state "Neither".

evidence.quote: Training reward curves for PPO on Llama-7B based models with the HH dataset.
Metrics are reported for the checkpoint with the highest test reward.

results.claim: RLOO (k=4) beats PPO on TL;DR by 10.3 win-rate points.
results.setup: TL;DR, Pythia-6.9B, GPT-4 judge vs reference SFT completions, checkpoint with highest test reward
results.quote: RLOO with k = 4 achieves the highest win-rates, outperforming PPO by 10.3, 14.5, and 32.1 for TL;DR, HH (Pythia) and HH (Llama), respectively.

results.claim: RLOO (k=4) beats PPO on HH (Pythia) by 14.5 points.
results.setup: Anthropic-HH, Pythia-6.9B, GPT-4 judge vs preferred completions
results.quote: outperforming PPO by 10.3, 14.5, and 32.1 for TL;DR, HH (Pythia) and HH (Llama), respectively

results.claim: RLOO (k=4) beats PPO on HH (Llama) by 32.1 points; PPO win-rate is only 32.0.
results.setup: Anthropic-HH, Llama-7B, GPT-4 judge vs preferred completions
results.quote: outperforming PPO by 10.3, 14.5, and 32.1 for TL;DR, HH (Pythia) and HH (Llama), respectively

results.claim: Win-rate table: RLOO (k=4) 77.9 on TL;DR vs DPO 66.6 and RAFT (k=4) 73.2.
results.note: Other cells: RLOO k=2 74.2, RAFT k=2 72.1, REINFORCE w/ baseline 70.7, Vanilla PG 70.4, PPO 67.6.

results.claim: REINFORCE with moving-average baseline matches or beats Vanilla PG, so partial completions need not be modelled.
results.setup: TL;DR, Pythia-6.9B; Vanilla PG 70.4; HH Pythia 37.9 vs 36.4; HH Llama 55.3 vs 52.3
results.quote: REINFORCE with baseline is on par with Vanilla PG on both TL;DR (70.7 vs 70.4) and HH (37.9 vs 36.4) datasets when using Pythia-based models.

results.claim: PPO loss is clipped on average less than 5% of the time per batch, so learning is near on-policy.
results.setup: all dataset and base-model pairings (stated); the clip ablation curves in Fig 1 are Llama-7B on HH
results.quote: We empirically found in our RLHF setting that the loss is actually clipped on average < 5% of the time per batch, throughout training across all dataset and base-model pairings

results.claim: Reward falls monotonically as GAE lambda decreases; lambda=1.0 (vanilla PG) is best.
results.setup: PPO, Llama-7B based model, HH dataset (Fig 1); lambda in {1.0, 0.95, 0.5, 0.0}
results.quote: We observe a monotonically decreasing reward with decreasing λ.

results.claim: RLOO with k=2 matches or beats RAFT with k=4, using half the online samples.
results.setup: all datasets and models; Pythia base noted in Fig 3 caption
results.quote: Noticeably, despite a smaller sampling budget, RLOOk=2 either closely matches or outperforms RAFTk=4, across all datasets and models.

results.claim: Averaged over three dataset-model pairs, RLOO win-rate is 61.3 (k=2) and 61.9 (k=4) vs RAFT 56.1 and 59.5.
results.quote: RLOO achieves win-rates of 61.3 and 61.9 for k = 2 and k = 4, respectively, while RAFT scores 56.1 and 59.5, respectively.

results.claim: On HH with Llama, DPO produces the longest generations and PPO the shortest.
results.note: Text says 104 and 16 tokens; Table 2 caption says 'Anthropic-HH dataset' and text says Llama-based models.

results.claim: REINFORCE with baseline gives 27% less reward variance than Vanilla PG.
results.quote: however, empirically results in 27% less variance

results.claim: RAFT is more sensitive than RLOO to higher KL weight (beta 0.25 to 1.0): lower reward and larger KL from reference.
results.quote: However increased regularization with β = {0.25, 0.5, 1.0}, not only RAFT is worse at optimizing the reward, but also deviates more from the reference policy.

results.claim: RAFT reward drops far more than RLOO under added reward noise sigma 3.0 and 5.0.
results.setup: Gaussian noise added to RM logits, sigma in {1.0,3.0,5.0}
results.quote: However, the drop is far more pronounced for RAFT with σ = {3.0, 5.0}

results.claim: In the SFT Llama model about 60% of probability mass sits on the single top token, and over 90% on the top 16.
results.setup: Llama SFT model used for HH, after the first generated token
results.quote: a significant (∼60%) portion of probability mass is put on only the single most probable token at each step

limits: Does not study reward model over-optimization (Gao et al., 2022).
Does not explore the LOO baseline in a per-token action framework with intermediary rewards.
Only simulated GPT-4 win-rates; no correlation with human evaluation measured.
No seeds, error bars or significance tests reported; single run per cell.
Only 6.9B and 7B models; PPO ablations in Fig 1 on Llama-7B HH only; code, hardware and compute not stated.
PPO win-rate on HH Llama (32.0) is very low, so the large gap may partly reflect PPO tuning (LR sweep only {1e-6, 1e-5}).

terms.definition: REINFORCE estimator applied to the trajectory return starting from each partial completion, with a learned baseline; equals PPO with lambda=1, no clipping, no ratio.
REINFORCE estimator applied to the full-trajectory return, treating the whole generation as a single action.
REINFORCE Leave-One-Out: k i.i.d. samples per prompt, each sample's baseline is the mean reward of the other k-1 samples.
